editorial:
Imagine you are stuck on a sunny island in the Mediterranean, but instead of a vacation, you are trapped in a huge house with a grumpy, dying millionaire. That is exactly where you find yourself with Flora Goforth, a wealthy woman who is just waiting for the end. Then enters Chris Flanders, a poet who basically hunts for rich people who are about to pass away so he can get their money. It feels like a weird game of cat and mouse where both people are trying to trick each other. The vibe is very strange and colorful, making you feel like you are watching a slow-motion car crash that you just cannot look away from.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the way the characters clash. It is not a fast movie, and some parts might feel a bit slow, but the tension is always there. If you enjoy stories about greed and people playing mind games, you will love this. You should definitely track down the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the bright colors of the island, or just look for it to rent on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: In the end, Sissy outsmarts Chris completely. After he spends the whole movie trying to manipulate her for her fortune, she reveals that she is not as frail as she looks. She kicks him out of her life and keeps her money. Instead of the vulture winning, the prey turns out to be the predator. He leaves empty-handed, proving that Sissy is way tougher and smarter than he ever gave her credit for.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and stories about rich people acting crazy.
